memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Then say to the Israelites: "Take a male goat for a sin offering, a calf and a lamb—both a year old and without defect—for a burnt offering, and an ox and a ram for a fellowship offering to sacrifice before the LORD, together with a grain offering mixed with olive oil. For today the LORD will appear to you."'" - Lev 9:3-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Four kinds of offering are gathered here: sin, burnt, fellowship, and grain. Everything Leviticus 1–7 described is brought together in one day.

And then comes the reason, stated plainly: For today the LORD will appear to you.

That is the promise the whole chapter turns on. All this preparation, all this careful obedience, is not an end in itself. It is because God is coming.

We can lose sight of this. Church attendance, Bible reading, prayer, service — these can quietly become the point, activities complete in themselves, boxes ticked. But every one of them exists for the same reason the offerings existed: because God meets with His people.

Jesus said something similar to the religious experts of His day: You study the Scriptures diligently because you think that in them you have eternal life. These are the very Scriptures that testify about me, yet you refuse to come to me (Jn 5:39-40).

The point of the practices is the Person.

Do not settle for tidy religious habits. God still comes to those who seek Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have my spiritual practices become ends in themselves rather than a means to knowing God?
2. Do I actually expect to meet with God when I come to Him?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, keep me from being satisfied with religious activity. I want You, not just habits about You. Amen.
